 'Abusive language': Yashveer Goud reveals why India celebrated fiercely after U19 Asia Cup final win over Pakistan

 Edited by Amit Kumar / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 13:29 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Image credit: BCCI India's celebrations after winning the U19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan were full of emotion. Now, young batter Yashveer Goud has revealed what led to the players' reactions after the memorable victory. Goud claimed that there was an exchange of words, including abusive language, when India lost to Pakistan in the group stage on Diwali. "We had lost the match on Diwali. There was some exchange of words between us, including abusive language. We couldn't say anything after losing that match. We were waiting for the final. We wanted to perform well and show what India is capable of," Goud told Sports Today. Watch Shreyas Iyer on India's series win, bowling brilliance, captaincy challenges and more 'Return bhi dena padta hai'
 Goud also explained why the Indian players celebrated the way they did after winning the final. According to him, they wanted to respond in the same manner as their Pakistani opponents had reacted after the group-stage match. "We were doing the same thing they had done. They were silent and we were silent too. We were wearing the proud Indian jersey. We were waiting for this moment. Return bhi dena padta hai. Everyone was emotional," he added. India had lost to Pakistan by three wickets in the group stage despite scoring 208. The defeat came on Diwali, making the loss even more disappointing for the young Indian team. India bounce back to beat Pakistan in dramatic final
 India had posted 208 in the group-stage match, with Arjun Rajput scoring an unbeaten 107 off just 85 balls. However, Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten 100 helped Pakistan recover from 61/5 and complete a three-wicket victory. India bounced back strongly in the semi-finals, beating Afghanistan by eight wickets. Captain Lakshya Raichandani led the way with 93 runs to set up another meeting with Pakistan in the final. Pakistan produced a strong batting performance in the title clash, scoring 337/9. Usman Khan led the charge with 107, while Abdul Qadir scored 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf contributed 63. India started their chase well, with Raichandani scoring 80 and Aaryavir Sehwag making 58. However, Pakistan fought back and left India struggling at 252/8. Join conversation

 Manal Chauhan kept India's hopes alive with 47 off 32 balls. But his dismissal at 309/9 left Mohit Ulva with just one wicket remaining. Ulva kept his calm and found support from Chigurupati Venkata. The pair added 30 runs for the last wicket to take India across the finish line. Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 balls as India reached 339/9 to register a thrilling one-wicket victory on the final ball. The win helped India dethrone Pakistan as U19 Asia Cup champions and completed a memorable comeback after their group-stage defeat. Poll Vote & Share your view
